description: A dessert shop is popular for their only two desserts - matcha ice cream and orange sorbet. Two units of flavouring and four units of ice cream is required to make one order of matcha ice cream. Four units of flavouring and three units of water is required to make an order of orange sorbet. The dessert shop has recently been getting more orders online for orange sorbet and therefore, there should be more orange sorbet made than matcha ice cream. However, at least fifteen percent of desserts made must be matcha ice cream. The dessert shop has available 600 units of ice cream and 550 units of water. How many of each dessert should the shop make to minimize the total amount of flavouring needed?

ResourceUsage.definition: Amount of each ingredient required to produce one unit of each dessert

AvailableIngredients.definition: Total available units of each ingredient

MinMatchaProportion.definition: Minimum proportion of desserts that must be matcha ice cream

objective.description: "Minimize the total amount of flavouring used to produce the matcha ice cream and orange sorbet"

constraints.description: 4 times the number of matcha ice creams produced should not exceed 600 units of ice cream
3 times the number of orange sorbets produced should not exceed 550 units of water
The number of orange sorbets produced should be greater than or equal to the number of matcha ice creams produced
The number of matcha ice creams produced should be at least 15 percent of the total number of desserts produced
The numbers of matcha ice creams and orange sorbets produced should be non-negative

MatchaQuantity.definition: Number of matcha ice cream orders produced

OrangeQuantity.definition: Number of orange sorbet orders produced
